# 09 Read the examples from disk instead of copying them

## Outcome

`index.test.ts` holds no copy of any `.srn` file. Every example test reads the real file, and one
test renders **every** file in `examples/` and asserts no error-severity diagnostics — so adding an
example gets it covered automatically, and editing one can fail a test.

## Why this ticket exists

Raised by the final review. `index.test.ts` carries six inline constants — `SEQUENCE_FULL_EXAMPLE_SOURCE`,
`CLASS_FULL_EXAMPLE_SOURCE` and four more — that duplicate `examples/*.srn` byte for byte, roughly
280 lines of copy. They are identical today and **nothing enforces it**: edit an example and the
tests keep passing against the stale copy, which is the opposite of what an example test is for.

Two examples, `complex-showcase.srn` and `step-reveal.srn`, are covered by no test at all.

The copies exist because `packages/core` cannot typecheck `node:fs` — no `@types/node`, and `lib`
is `["ES2022", "DOM"]`. That constraint is now lifted: the dependency is authorized.

Note `vite.config.ts` already imports `node:url` and gets away with it only because `tsconfig`'s
`include` is `["src"]`, so it is never typechecked. Tests live in `src/`, so they cannot dodge it
the same way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `@types/node` is a devDependency of `packages/core`, and `tsc --noEmit` stays clean.
- [x] All six inline `*_EXAMPLE_SOURCE` constants are deleted. Each test that used one reads the
      corresponding `examples/*.srn` from disk instead.
- [x] Resolve the path relative to the test file. **This criterion's literal form was wrong** and
      the worker corrected it: Vite statically rewrites `new URL(<string literal>, import.meta.url)`
      into a dev-server asset URL that `readFileSync` refuses. `import.meta.url` must go through a
      binding first. Originally written as `new URL("../../../examples/x.srn", import.meta.url)`,
      not from `process.cwd()` — the suite must pass whether run from the repo root or from
      `packages/core`. Verify both, do not assume.
- [x] One test enumerates `examples/` at runtime and renders every `.srn` in it, asserting zero
      error-severity diagnostics for each. It must **fail** if a new example is added that does not
      render — prove this by temporarily adding a broken `.srn`, observing the failure, and deleting
      it. Report that evidence.
- [x] That test names the file in its failure output, so a failure says which example broke.
- [x] `complex-showcase.srn` and `step-reveal.srn` are consequently covered.
- [x] A test proves the drift guard works: change nothing, but confirm that the sequence-full
      timeline test now reads the real file — e.g. by asserting a string only the file contains.
- [x] Every existing assertion about example content still passes. This ticket changes where the
      source comes from, not what is asserted about it.

## Test seam

`render()` in `index.test.ts`, unchanged. Only the source of the input moves.

## Write ownership

- `packages/core/package.json`
- `packages/core/tsconfig.json` (only if `@types/node` needs an explicit `types` entry)
- `packages/core/src/index.test.ts`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`

Do **not** edit any `.srn` file. If a test fails because an example is genuinely broken, that is a
finding to report, not to fix here.

## Shared resources

None — runs alone.

Nothing. The board's other eight tickets are all done.
